ops.en: THE PRESSURE. ve-ha-raav KAVED ba-aretz — the span's shortest verse is its engine: the heaviness (kaved) that will overturn a father's refusal; gen_64's decree (41:31 'very heavy') verified at Canaan's door.

A STANDING TABLE COUNTS THIS OPENING VERSE [claim G66-34]. The paved-way machine - eleven matched pairs by which the ancestor's descent prefigures the nation's - names this severe famine beside the ancestor's own. The block opens inside a pattern the corpus has been carrying since its twenty-eighth unit, and the membership is enumerated rather than asserted. [folded shape: kept record]

THE BARE DEMAND [G66-03]. SHUVU shivru lanu MEAT okhel — return, buy a LITTLE: the father's minimal plan, pushed as if Benjamin were not the price; Judah's next speech will show it impossible, and Jacob's own zot-asu (43:11) will supersede it — the dead-by-revision class gains its second member, and this time the reviser is the father himself (gen_65's was the governor). shuvu written LEAN per the…

THE WARNING CITED. HAED HEID banu ha-ish — the doubled witness-verb (the testimony idiom of the law units) wraps gen_65's still-open carrying demand: lo tiru fanai bilti achikhem itkhem — the face- condition quoted verbatim-shaped, twice in this chapter (43:3, 43:5): Judah argues from the queue.

THE CONDITION [G66-05]. im yeshkha meshaleach... NERDA — 'we will go down': the form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — here and Babel's 'let US go down and confuse' (11:7, the divine plural of gen_25) [VERIFIED: manifest G66-05]; the Masorah's third is Saul's night- pursuit (1 Sam 14:36, named): the Kitzur reads the three descents into one — a going-down that scatters, a going-down that pursues,…

THE REFUSAL-CONDITION. ve-im enkha meshaleach LO NERED — Judah states the strike: the face-clause repeats word for word (the quoted demand is now the brothers' shield), and the father's bare demand (43:2) stands exposed as unexecutable.

THE REPROACH. lama HAREOTEM li — the do-ill verb in the father's mouth; the narrator shifts to ISRAEL for the whole negotiation (43:6, 8, 11 — the covenant name presiding over the release of the covenant's youngest).

THE DOUBLED ASKING [G66-06, G66-07]. SHAOL shaal — the infinitive FULL with its vav (the Hilleli and every precise book; its Samuel pair named) — and the skeleton's Torah census is a collision worth the filing: the asking (here), the Edomite king Shaul (36:37-38), and SHEOL the pit (Deut 32:22) — four full tokens: to ask, a king, and the grave [VERIFIED: manifest G66-06]. ha-YADOA neda — 'could we…

THE SEND-DEMAND. SHILCHA ha-naar iti — Judah's imperative pushed at the father: the lad-word for the grown Benjamin (the father's eyes kept in the grammar); ve-nichye ve-lo namut — Jacob's own live-and- not-die clause (42:2) handed back to him with its census tripled: gam anachnu gam ata gam tapenu — we, you, the little ones (the gimel of gam dageshed per MS, asserted [G66-12]).

THE SURETY. anokhi EERVENU — the pledge-verb (arav) Judah once used for a kid and a cord (38:17-18, gen_61): now he pledges HIMSELF for the brother; mi-yadi TEVAQSHENU — the require-verb of the blood- handler (9:5, gen_21) volunteered against his own hand. Reuben staked two sons and was refused (42:37); Judah stakes his standing and will be heard — the machine files the contrast, and 44:32 will ca…

A NARRATIVE PLEDGE MATCHED PIECE BY PIECE TO A LAW-PROVERB [claim G66-25]. The surety, the handshake, and the snare of one's own mouth are each mapped to a clause of this verse, and the deliverance read as cleaving to the dust of the man's feet. Onkelos supplies the register the whole reading needs, using the technical word for SECURITY - without it the pledge is only a promise. A six-item practic…

THE LINGERING [G66-04]. ki LULE hitmahmahnu — the had-not word written with a FINAL ALEF, its only such token in the Torah (the yod-form stands twice: Laban's field 31:42, the enemy's boast Deut 32:27 — both asserted) [VERIFIED: manifest G66-04]; and the Kitzur reads the seam: the last letters of ki ata SHAVNU ze — the four- letter Name in order (asserted by the builder): the Name accompanies the …

THE RULE'S RECORDED COUNTEREXAMPLE SITS AT THIS VERSE [claim G66-34]. The standing rule that the conditional particle always marks the merit of the patriarchs meets here the one case that resists it - a delay is not a merit - and the corpus keeps both the objection and its harmonization: even the delay and the ascent ran on that merit. The counterexample is not deleted from the rule's own dossier.…

THE REVISION. im ken efo ZOT ASU — the father adopts the governor's own formula (42:18's zot asu): the bare demand of 43:2 is superseded by a caravan-plan — gift, double silver, the brother — and the machine leaves 43:2 OPEN forever, dead by its author's revision. The six kinds (balm, honey, gum, ladanum, pistachios, almonds) against the six sons of the mistresses per the Kitzur (named); botnim ('…

A RARE WORD WHOSE WHOLE GENESIS CAREER IS THE DECEPTION AND THIS VERSE [claim G66-24, machine-checked]. The chain reads the father's 'if SO, then do this' against the trembling 'WHO then was it' of the stolen blessing - measure for measure at the identical particle. Machine-checked: the word stands at exactly FOUR Torah seats, and three of them are these two scenes, two in the blessing chapter and…

THE DOUBLE. ve-khesef MISHNE — double silver: the Kitzur's pair rides the doubled word to the doubled repayment (named); ve-et ha- kesef HA-MUSHAV — 'the RETURNED silver': hold the participle — 43:18 will write its clipped twin (ha-shav) and the erring copies will harmonize the two [G66-09, armed]; ulai MISHGE hu — 'perhaps an error': the father supplies the innocent reading the sons feared to cla…

THE RELEASE [G66-03]. ve-et ACHIKHEM qachu — the withheld son released in four words; ve-qumu SHUVU — and the return-verb here is written FULL: the same chapter that wrote shuvu lean at the bare demand (43:2) writes it full at the release — and the full imperative stands three tokens in the Torah's skeleton-count (14:17's noun 'his return' collides in the skeleton, framed), the Ramah naming this, …

THE PRAYER. ve-EL SHADAY yiten lakhem RACHAMIM — the father pushes a demand on God by the Almighty-name (the name of the covenant- blessings, 17:1, 35:11): mercy before the man, the other brother, and Benjamin. The queue holds it OPEN: Simeon walks out at 43:23 (the partial the prose records), Benjamin's release is two units away — a prayer paced slower than its span. BINYAMIN full (the seven-full…

PETITION BEGINS WHERE CALCULATION IS EXHAUSTED [claim G66-26]. 'At the time of finding' is opened four ways, and this prayer is placed at the fourth - the completion of THE ACCOUNTING: when he saw there was nothing further he could do for his sons, he poured out supplications. That is the model for why the blessing comes at this verse and not earlier. [folded shape: kept record]

THE SAME WORDS READ AS A FATHER'S PRAYER AND AS A NATION'S [claim G66-27]. Plainly: 'the man' is the Egyptian ruler, the other brother is the one held, and the bereavement is of two sons. In the exile reading: 'the man' is the Holy One, the other brother is the ten tribes, 'and Benjamin' the two remaining, the doubled bereavement the two destructions - closing 'I shall not be bereaved again.' Neit…

THE SENDING DONE. ve-et BINYAMIN — the lad is in the caravan: Judah's send-demand discharges (and the spelling turns LEAN the moment the son leaves the father's holding — 43:15's binyamin against 43:14's full, the census's own hinge, asserted).

THE PLAN EXECUTED. va-yiqchu... et ha-mincha ha-ZOT u-mishne kesef laqchu... — the verse walks the father's verbs verbatim (take, take, and down): the caravan-plan discharges; va-yaamdu lifne YOSEF — and the standing-before closes gen_65's distance in five words. ha-zot with the zayin dageshed per MS (checked [G66-12]); u-MISHNE kesef — the doubled-silver word once so in the Torah (asserted under …

THE HOUSE-ORDER. HAVE et ha-anashim ha-baita u-tvoach TEVACH ve- hakhen — bring, slaughter, prepare: the governor's noon-order pushed on the house-steward; va-yar yosef ITAM et BINYAMIN — the seeing that triggers it is the census's fourth full station (43:16, asserted under G65-02).

A LATER STATUTE READ BACKWARD INTO A NARRATIVE VERB [claim G66-31]. 'Slaughter and PREPARE' is bound by equal-decree to the manna instruction, preparation being a Sabbath word - so the meal at this verse is held to be a Sabbath meal, generations before the commandment. Onkelos reads the same clause's hour as the day's PRINCIPAL MEAL rather than a clock time; the two readings sit beside each other …
THE RECEIPT. va-yaas ha-ish KA-ASHER AMAR yosef — the as-Joseph-said clause (gen_64's verification-grammar, 41:54) pops the house-order in one verse: the steward is the span's cleanest executor.

THE FEAR [G66-08, G66-09, G66-13]. va-YIRU — written with BOTH yods (the Hilleli alone clips one; the Yerushalmi, every book, Rashi's own note, and the Masorah's all-Torah-full rule stand against it) [VERIFIED: manifest G66-08]. ha-kesef HA-SHAV — the clipped returned-word: copies that write ha-MUSHAV here (harmonizing 43:12) err per MS — the letter keeps the father's participle and the sons' apar…

AN INARTICULATE FEAR CONVERTED INTO AN ACCURATE LEGAL FORECAST [claim G66-29]. Two obscure idioms become two named harms - to LORD IT OVER US and to FRAME US - and both are exactly what the planted goblet is about to deliver. The unit's threat operators can name the harms instead of gesturing at them. [folded shape: dual-track translation]

THE THRESHOLD. va-yigshu — the draw-near verb (Judah will wear it as a crown at 44:18): the confession is made at the DOOR, before the house can swallow them — the machine notes the placement as the speech's own caution.

THE DOUBLED DESCENT. YAROD YARADNU — the infinitive-doubling (as the man's asking was doubled, 43:7): the brothers' speech mirrors the interrogation's grammar; bi adoni — the plea-word of supplication (44:18 will open with it).

THE COMPRESSION. kaspenu be-MISHKALO — by its very weight (the honesty-detail added to the telling); and the report folds the two discoveries (one at the lodging, 42:27; nine at the emptying, 42:35) into ONE lodging-scene: the retelling variance-file's neatest compression, filed as letter-fact.
THE NOT-KNOWING. lo yadanu MI SAM — the confession ends at the exact edge of their knowledge: the machine files the who-question as the speech's open slot (the steward answers it with God, 43:23).

FEAR NOT. shalom lakhem AL TIRAU — the steward pushes the calm as a negative demand (the corpus's fear-not class, gen_58's midwife): no receipt follows — it stands open as such words do. Elohekhem v-elohe avikhem natan lakhem MATMON — the treasure-word (its one Torah token, asserted): Egypt's steward hands the brothers the first theology of the plot they will ever hear — and it is the true one tol…
THE PROTOCOL. mayim... raglehem... mispo — the Abraham-triple (18:4-5's water and feet; 24:32's fodder) performed by Egypt's steward: the hospitality grammar of the fathers in the house of the son.

THE STAGING. va-yakhinu et ha-MINCHA — the gift-word (mincha) that pacified Esau (32:14-21, gen_55) is staged again for a wronged brother: the machine files the pattern-echo; ad BO yosef ba- tzahorayim — the noon appointment kept.

THE ELEVEN BOW [G66-01; gen_60 ARMED]. va-yishtachavu LO ARTZA — with Benjamin present the count is ELEVEN: the second dream's eleven stars (37:9) step into the ledger beside the sheaves; and the bringing-verb va-yaviu (43:26) carries the Masorah's rarest mark — a DAGESH IN THE ALEF, one of its four dageshed alefs (its Ezra partner named), and SNAPSHOT writes the dot in the guttural in-stream [VER…

THE INQUIRY. ha-SHALOM avikhem ha-zaqen — the governor's first question is the father: the still-alive phrase (ha-odenu chai) that will detonate at 45:3 (ha-od avi chai) is rehearsed here in the mask's voice.

THE CLIPPED BOW [G66-02]. va-yiqdu VA-YISHTACHU (written) / va- yishtachavu (read) — the span's own ketiv/qere lands on the BOW- WORD: the writing clips the final vav, the reading restores it — and SNAPSHOT carries the pair as two tokens in-stream, the bare written form beside the pointed read form (the verse's token-count wears the doubling) [VERIFIED: manifest G66-02]: at the second bowing, the …

A COUNT WHOSE OWN HEDGE WORD IS CONFIRMED BY THE INK [claim G66-21, machine-checked]. The chain bills an early death to the silences - ALMOST FIVE TIMES the brother said 'your servant my father' in his hearing and he said nothing. Machine-checked: FOUR seats carry the phrase in the identical bare form, all in the next block; the FIFTH is this verse, where both words take a prefixed preposition. Fi…

THE BLESSING [G66-10]. Elohim YACHNEKHA beni — the grace-verb stands ONCE so in the Torah [VERIFIED: manifest G66-10]; the priestly benediction will conjugate it with a vav (ויחנך, 'and be gracious to you', Num 6:25 — collision framed, named), and the Kitzur pairs it with the grace-cry of Isaiah (named): the governor blesses the only full brother with the priests' verb before the priests exist. be…

A LEDGER OPENED MANY BLOCKS BACK CLOSES HERE [claim G66-32]. The grace-census recorded eleven brothers blessed with grace in the father's word and Benjamin's withheld; the deferral it named is discharged at this verse - by the brother he does not yet recognize, not by the father. Onkelos stops on the same half-verse for its own reason, rendering the blessing as graciousness FROM BEFORE THE LORD. A…

THE SECOND WEEPING. ki NIKHMERU rachamav — the compassion-verb that burns (its one narrative kindling); va-yavo ha-CHADRA va-yevk SHAMA — the weep-series' second station (42:24 turned away; now a chamber contains it): the mask requires architecture.

THE RESTRAINT [G66-10]. va-YITAPAQ — the restrain-verb stands ONCE in the Torah [VERIFIED: manifest G66-10, asserted]; its Scripture- pair is Haman restraining himself (Esther 5:10, named — the Kitzur: both restraints open in sorrow and end in joy, each for its own house). simu LACHEM — the governor's shortest demand: two words, pushed.

THE PARTITIONED TABLE. va-YASIMU lo levado — the set-verb answers in the next breath (the span's third one-verse discharge); levado... levadam... levadam — three alones at one meal: the abomination- clause (toeva) files Egypt's own purity-law as narrative fact — the Hebrews eat apart in the house of the Hebrew.

THE SEPARATE TABLES GET THEIR CAUSE FROM THE TRANSLATION [claim G66-28]. Onkelos does not render the taboo word; it states the reason - THE ANIMAL THE EGYPTIANS WORSHIP, THE HEBREWS EAT. The largest expansion in the block, and it means the unit's separation operator carries a cult conflict the Hebrew never names. [folded shape: dual-track translation]

THE SEATING [G66-10]. ha-BEKHOR ki-vkhorato ve-ha-TZAIR ki-tzeirato — twelve men seated by a stranger in exact birth order: va-yitmehu — they wondered (the cup-divination prop the readings hang here, named); ve-ha-tzair stands ONCE so in the Torah (asserted; Isaiah's mighty-younger named): the younger the verse seats low is the one the table will honor five-fold.

A BANQUET DETAIL READ AS EVIDENCE OF A CONFRONTATION NOT YET NARRATED [claim G66-33]. 'The kings convened, they passed together' is read as the two brothers, with 'passed' heard as filled with FURY, and 'they saw and were astonished' as this verse - the tribes standing out of it: kings contend with kings, what is that to us. Onkelos makes the seating deliberate, rendering it that they were SEATED …

FIVE HANDS [G66-11]. va-TEREV masat BINYAMIN mi-masot kulam CHAMESH yadot — the mother's son lifted five-fold (the readings count the five garments of 45:22 forward, named); MI-MASOT written LEAN with the Hilleli, the old print, and every precise copy against the erring printer — the Masorah's four-token portion-file: the two of THIS verse lean, its two other stations full [VERIFIED: manifest G66-…

A CLAIM ABOUT TWENTY-TWO YEARS OF TWO PARTIES' CONDUCT, RESTING ON THE LAST WORD OF THE VERSE [claims G66-22 and G66-23, both machine-checked]. Through all the years apart neither he nor they tasted wine, and the proof is 'they drank and became drunk WITH HIM' - with him they drank, without him they did not. Machine-checked: that word stands once in the verse, in final position, exactly where the …
